transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recorded)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Ramos (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (CTO, Juniper), Marco Alvarez (Head of ML), Priya Singh (Infra Lead), Ethan Park (Procurement)

Summary:
Juniper is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and dedicated capacity to support a new chat-assistant and batch embedding pipelines. Primary drivers: predictable unit cost, staying within a strict monthly budget, and meeting 95th percentile latency targets for user chat (sub-350ms server-side target). They want to understand per-token pricing levers, the impact of batching and KV prefix caching on unit economics, residency/VPC options for PII-sensitive flows, and an initial pilot scope.

Topics covered:
- Current token burn and TPS (Q1 baseline)
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison and billing buckets
- Batching, KV cache, and prefix caching tradeoffs
- Private/VPC requirements, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope, timelines, and stakeholders

Action items (captured during call):
- Sofia to share pilot pricing spreadsheet and an example cost model using Juniper's Q1 burn figures
- Dev to prepare a bench plan for batching + cache tests and run initial latency sims
- Juniper to share token burn and traffic shape

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ramos: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Quick roll call, I have Dev here with me, and from Juniper I see Lena, Marco, Priya and Ethan. Can everyone hear ok?
[00:10] Lena Cho: Yep, we're good. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:14] Sofia Ramos: Great. High level — we're here to unpack the cost side of things, per-token economics, why folks choose hosted vs dedicated, and what a pilot might look like. Dev will cover some technical levers. Marco, do you want to ground us in what you're running today?
[00:28] Marco Alvarez: Yeah, sure. Quick context — we run a customer-facing chat assistant plus nightly embedding jobs. Chat is low-latency, heavy on short-context prompts, average turn is around 70 tokens. Embeddings are batch, sometimes millions per night but not latency sensitive. Right now it's an internal self-hosted stack using mixed GPUs; we're seeing big variance in cost and ops overhead.
[00:48] Priya Singh: Also worth flagging infra constraint — security team wants keys in our KMS for PII flows and audit logs for queries tied to accounts.
[00:56] Dev Patel: That's useful. For cost levers at inference time, the main ones are model choice (smaller vs larger), batching, and cache/prefix reuse. Batching increases throughput and lowers per-token GPU overhead but can add tail latency; cache and prefix KV reuse can reduce repeated computation for shared prefixes or instruction prompts.
[01:18] Marco Alvarez: Can you give a rough example? Like we have 40k daily active users, avg 1.8 chats per day, peak TPS around 120 requests sustained for a few minutes.
[01:29] Dev Patel: With those numbers, batching and a dedicated pool usually make sense to hit lower cost per token. Example: in hosted mode, you pay per-token at published rates — but with smart batching and prefix cache we can reduce effective tokens computed on the GPU by 20-45% depending on prompt patterns. In dedicated, you pre-reserve capacity which spreads fixed GPU cost over volume — so per-token can be lower if you hit utilization.
[01:53] Ethan Park: Budget wise, we have a cap of $35k/month for the AI stack in year one. That includes both chat and nightly embeddings. Does a dedicated commitment fit that?
[02:03] Sofia Ramos: It depends on utilization. A small dedicated pool might be expensive if you underutilize. We can run a hybrid where high-priority chat runs on dedicated and batch embeddings run on hosted burst capacity. That gives predictability for the chat SLA while keeping embeddings cost-flexible.
[02:20] Lena Cho: Two parts I'm worried about — one is the per-token billing granularity and second is how caching affects billing. If the cache avoids compute, do you still pay for the tokens?
[02:32] Dev Patel: Good question. Billing is per-request tokens for hosted; however, effective GPU token compute can be reduced by cache hits — Redwood's platform can report token-level compute vs billed tokens in the console so you can see delta. For dedicated, since you pay for reservation, billing is not per token but you're still concerned about unit economics per effective token.
[02:52] Marco Alvarez: So we might see billed tokens higher than computed tokens on the GPU if client-side concatenation sends full context even if the runtime serves from KV?
[03:00] Dev Patel: Exactly — that's why we recommend sanitizing prompts and using prefix tokens on the server side. We also offer an optimization that strips repeated instruction prefixes before billing calculations — depends on integration. I'll follow up with docs.
[03:12] Priya Singh: On private deployment — we need VPC and customer-managed KMS. Also, SOC 2 is required. Are those available?
[03:21] Sofia Ramos: Yes — Private supports VPC, KMS integrations, and audit logs. We have SOC 2 reports we can share. For some air-gapped customers we do a deployed control plane, but that has different pricing and longer lead times.
[03:36] Ethan Park: Lead times matter — procurement asks 8–10 week timelines for private. If we do a pilot, can it be hosted first and then move to private?
[03:44] Sofia Ramos: Absolutely; hosted pilot to validate unit economics and integration, then lift-and-shift to private when you're ready. We typically recommend a 4–6 week hosted pilot.
[03:52] Marco Alvarez: Let's talk numbers — rough per-token published rate for hosted? Give a baseline for chat model and embed model.
[03:58] Sofia Ramos: For reference, hosted text gen is X.XX per 1k tokens for base open models in our catalog, and embeddings are Y.YY per 1k embedding units — for this conversation I'll share a tailored spreadsheet. The exact numbers vary with model and quantization.
[04:14] Marco Alvarez: The specifics are crucial. Our embeddings run at night and could cost a lot if per-embedding unit is not competitive.
[04:21] Dev Patel: Another lever — quantized model variants on dedicated can reduce memory and increase throughput, improving cost. But quantization might slightly affect output quality for some prompts, so we recommend running a small eval set.
[04:34] Lena Cho: Is there a way to simulate cost before committing? Like run a 1-week trial against production traffic?
[04:40] Sofia Ramos: Yes — we can do a short pilot where you route X% of traffic or replay logs into a sandbox. We can provide cost reports and top-line per-token effective costs. We'll want the traffic shape and sample prompts.
[04:53] Priya Singh: Replaying logs we need to scrub PII — are there tooling/helpers?
[04:57] Dev Patel: We have scripts and guidance. Also recommend tokenizing first and sending hashed ids for evaluation. We'll share an example.
[05:06] Marco Alvarez: On batching — you mentioned tail latency. Our SLO is 95th percentile server-side <350ms. If batching increases throughput but pushes p95 to 500ms, not acceptable. How does Redwood balance that?
[05:19] Dev Patel: We tune batch sizes with latency-aware policies. Continuous batching waits up to a small window (5–25ms) for more requests before executing, but you can set strict latency SLOs that enforce smaller batch sizes or dedicated shards for low-latency routes. There's a tradeoff — smaller batch -> higher per-token cost. We can model the sensitivity based on your peak shapes.
[05:40] Lena Cho: Do you support route-level policies? We want user-facing chat to always hit low-latency pool and background tasks to use cost-optimized pool.
[05:46] Sofia Ramos: Yes — route-level model assignment and routing policies are standard. You can pin chat to dedicated low-latency, embeddings to hosted or a separate dedicated pool with different scaling.
[05:55] Ethan Park: Procurement question — how is overage billed if we set reserved capacity? Monthly reconciliation?
[06:00] Sofia Ramos: Reserved capacity contracts include a committed baseline and overage rates. Overage billing is monthly and we can set alerts/quotas. We can also configure burst capacity to avoid failures without long-term commitment.
[06:11] Priya Singh: For audit purposes, we need request-level logs and redaction controls. Does private deployment keep logs on-prem?
[06:18] Dev Patel: Private can integrate with your logging stack and keep logs within your VPC; you control retention and redaction. Hosted options have configurable retention and export.
[06:27] Marco Alvarez: I want to understand the math — if we take our baseline: 40k DAU, 1.8 chats/day, avg 70 tokens per turn, that's roughly X tokens per month. Can you walk through a sample cost model?
[06:40] Sofia Ramos: Sure — (on the fly) 40k * 1.8 interactions * let's say 3 turns per interaction * 70 tokens = 40k * 1.8 * 3 * 70 = 15,120,000 tokens/month just for chat. Embeddings maybe 2M per night * embedding unit cost. We'll build a spreadsheet with those rows and compare hosted rates vs dedicated amortized GPU cost given utilization assumptions.
[07:07] Marco Alvarez: Ok, that 15M number helps. If caching reduces compute by 30% on average, effective compute tokens drop to ~10.6M.
[07:16] Dev Patel: Exactly — and with batching you might decrease GPU cost per token further. We'll simulate three scenarios: no cache/no batching (baseline), cache only, cache + aggressive batching.
[07:27] Lena Cho: For the pilot, we're trying to keep spend under $10k for the month. Is that realistic to validate both chat and embeddings?
[07:35] Sofia Ramos: For a limited pilot, yes. We can scope a smaller traffic slice (e.g., 10% chat traffic + sample of embeddings) to stay within $10k. That would show the direction of savings and let you test KV caching.
[07:46] Marco Alvarez: What's the data flow change for implementing prefix caching? I want to avoid massive client changes.
[07:51] Dev Patel: There are two patterns: client-side minimal change where you send full context and we do server-side canonicalization and prefix stripping; or a smarter client-side where you send only deltas. Server-side is easiest for pilots — requires integration hooks and testing.
[08:05] Priya Singh: Does server-side prefix stripping affect billing visibility or compliance? We need an auditable trail of original inputs.
[08:12] Sofia Ramos: We can keep originals in an encrypted audit log with controlled access so you have the trail but avoid repeated compute.
[08:20] Ethan Park: About SLA — you mentioned 99.9% for dedicated? Is that standard?
[08:25] Sofia Ramos: We offer SLA tiers. Dedicated pools can be backed by higher SLAs with faster support response times. We'll include the SLA matrix in the docs we send.
[08:34] Marco Alvarez: Any examples of customers that moved from hosted pilot to dedicated and the delta they saw?
[08:40] Dev Patel: Yes — a fintech customer moved chat to a small dedicated pool and saw 35% reduction in per-token effective cost after tuning batching and using quantized models. They retained hosted for infrequent heavy batch tasks. I'll anonymize and share the case study.
[08:54] Lena Cho: On security again — if we go private later, what changes in the migration? Data pipeline, KMS keys, and network rules? Any downtime?
[09:03] Sofia Ramos: Migration is planned — typically a cutoff window and testing. We coordinate with your infra team to set up VPC peering, KMS rotation, and run smoke tests. We aim for zero data loss; downtime is minimal but we'll schedule a maintenance window if needed.
[09:16] Marco Alvarez: About quantization — for our chat prompts, we care about subtle phrasing. How do you validate quality delta?
[09:22] Dev Patel: We run evals on your prompt set — compare embeddings similarity and generative quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/qualitative review). For chat we recommend A/B testing on a small user cohort.
[09:32] Priya Singh: Procurement asks for a trial contract — can we get a short-term MOU for a hosted pilot?
[09:38] Sofia Ramos: Yes, we can do a 30–60 day pilot MOU with defined scope and a capped spend. We'll have legal coordinate.
[09:46] Ethan Park: Any hidden fees — data egress or logging extras?
[09:50] Sofia Ramos: We'll be explicit. Hosted includes standard ingress/egress up to typical limits; large export or long retention of logs can be add-ons. We'll call those out in the pricing sheet.
[09:59] Marco Alvarez: For the tech deep-dive next week, I'd like Dev to show a microbenchmark that mirrors our 120 TPS spikes. Can we configure a dedicated pool sized for that?
[10:08] Dev Patel: Yes — we'll draft a bench plan that models spike shapes and batch sensitivity. We'll recommend pool sizes and autoscale params.
[10:16] Lena Cho: Ok, last thing — timeline. If we sign pilot in a week, can the hosted pilot start in two weeks?
[10:22] Sofia Ramos: Yes, two weeks is feasible for hosted. Private will take longer.
[10:27] Sofia Ramos: All right, quick recap and next steps — Sofia will send the pricing spreadsheet and example cost model by Monday 5/24; Dev will send the bench plan and sample scripts by Tuesday 5/26; Juniper will share token burn and traffic shapes by Friday 5/22. We'll schedule a 60-minute technical benchmark session for 5/27. Everyone ok?
[10:45] Lena Cho: Sounds good. Thank you.
[10:48] Marco Alvarez: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:50] Priya Singh: Thanks.
[10:52] Ethan Park: Thanks all.

End of recording.
